blockFields: `alerts` (list of `{ "name" (the alert name as in the rules file), "problem" (what is wrong with it today), "change" (the concrete new rule: expression, threshold, duration or routing), "severity" ("page", "ticket" or "remove") }`), `keep` (list of alert names that are fine as they are).
kindExtra: Seed 14 to 20 alert rules in a rules file; 6 or 7 of them are flawed in ways the 30-day firing history and the metrics show (a page on a cause such as CPU that never matched user impact; a threshold below normal daily peak so it fires every evening; no duration so it flaps; a rule on a metric name that no longer exists; a duplicate of another rule; a page that should be a ticket; a symptom with no runbook link that was acked and ignored 40 times). The rest are sound decoys, including one noisy-looking rule that caught every real outage. Key shape: per flawed alert a `some` item on `alerts` matching its `name` by `field` and the right problem keywords (two patterns), plus `none` items so a sound alert listed for removal fails, and an `every` item that each listed change names a metric that exists (`inSet` on a metrics catalogue file where it applies). 14 to 18 items.
brief: Phase: release, ops and on-call. Role: SRE. Folder: the monitoring repo of a mid-size web product: alert rules (YAML), the metrics catalogue, 30 days of alert firing history (CSV: alert, start, end, acked by, linked incident), the incident list for the month, the on-call handoff notes and the runbook index. On-call people are burning out from pages. The request from the on-call lead: review the alerts, say which ones to change or remove and how, and which to keep.
